name: Irving
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Irving, TX 2026
seo_description: Kids' Christmas in Irving, TX: Holidays at Heritage parade and tree lighting, free Santa photos, Santa at Irving Arts Center and Mandalay Canal lights.
lede: The story of Christmas in Irving begins with a town born in Christmas week, at a lot auction on December 19, 1903, and today it centers on Heritage Park downtown, where the city holds its Holidays at Heritage parade and tree lighting. Up north in Las Colinas, Irving Arts Center has hung its Holiday Tree Exhibition for 34 years, and the Mandalay Canal glows on December Saturdays.
sections: A railroad town born in Christmas week

Irving began with a railroad survey. In the fall of 1902, J.O. Schulze and Otis Brown were working on a survey crew for the Chicago, Rock Island and Gulf Railway between Dallas and Fort Worth when they decided to start a town along the planned line. They bought 80 acres from rancher Henry Britain and launched Irving with a lot auction on December 19, 1903, six days before Christmas. Residents voted to incorporate in 1914, and in 1920 the town still had only 357 people. The city dedicated Centennial Park on October 3, 2003, with statues of the two founders, a short walk from Heritage Park where Irving now lights its Christmas tree.

Heritage Park on South Main Street keeps Irving's oldest pieces in one place: the city's first water tower, windmill and library, the Caster Cabin from 1887 and a replica of the 1903 Rock Island Depot. Each December the City of Irving turns the park into Holidays at Heritage, three free Saturdays that start with a lighted parade through the Heritage District and a tree lighting with a drone light show. In 2025 the parade theme was Unwrap the Magic, and the drone show lit the sky at 8:30 pm. The following Saturdays bring a family movie on the lawn and a morning of free photos with Santa at the park gazebo.

Irving exists because of the Rock Island line, and trains still stop in the old downtown. The Trinity Railway Express, the commuter train between Dallas and Fort Worth, stops at the Downtown Irving/Heritage Crossing station at 201 Rock Island Road, a short walk from Heritage Park, so families can ride the train to the parade. In Las Colinas, the DART Orange Line connects Irving with downtown Dallas and DFW Airport. For a bigger train day, the McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley runs vintage streetcars in Dallas, and the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano and the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco show the trains that built North Texas.
celebrates: Irving celebrates in two places. Downtown, the City of Irving's Holidays at Heritage fills Heritage Park on three December Saturdays with a lighted parade, a tree lighting and drone show, an outdoor holiday movie and free photos with Santa at the gazebo. In Las Colinas, Irving Arts Center hangs its annual Holiday Tree Exhibition in free galleries and welcomes Santa on Saturday afternoons, while the Las Colinas Association lights the trees along the Mandalay Canal with live music and free cocoa. The Ritz-Carlton Dallas, Las Colinas adds a lobby tree lighting, teas with Santa and gingerbread decorating.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Irving's Holidays at Heritage parade rolled through the Heritage District on Saturday, December 6, under the theme Unwrap the Magic. The evening ended in Heritage Park with the tree lighting and a drone light show at 8:30 pm. The city invited decorated floats, vehicles and walking groups to apply for the parade, as it did again for 2026, when the theme became Stars, Stripes and Holiday Lights.
facts: Irving was launched with a lot auction on December 19, 1903, so the city's birthday falls in Christmas week. Its founders, J.O. Schulze and Otis Brown, met as surveyors for the Chicago, Rock Island and Gulf Railway. Heritage Park, where the city tree is lit, preserves Irving's first water tower, windmill and library and the 1887 Caster Cabin. Irving Arts Center's Holiday Tree Exhibition reached its 34th year in 2026, with a Holiday Time Machine theme.
trains: The Trinity Railway Express stops at the Downtown Irving/Heritage Crossing station at 201 Rock Island Road, close to Heritage Park and the Holidays at Heritage events, and it runs east to Dallas Union Station and west to Fort Worth. The DART Orange Line serves Las Colinas and DFW Airport. Nearby train attractions include the McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley in Dallas, the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano and the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco.

traditions: Holidays at Heritage parade and tree lighting
The City of Irving's lighted parade through the Heritage District ends with the city tree and a drone show in Heritage Park; in 2026 it is Saturday, December 5.
Free photos with Santa at the gazebo
On the last Holidays at Heritage Saturday, December 19, 2026, Santa sits at the Heritage Park gazebo and families get a printed and digital photo for free.
Irving Arts Center fills its free galleries with decorated trees every December, and the tree with the most Facebook likes wins a cash prize.
Merry and Bright Nights on the Mandalay Canal
The Las Colinas Association lights the canal trees with music and complimentary cocoa on December 5, 12 and 19, 2026.
Santa Saturdays at Irving Arts Center
Santa makes cards and crafts with kids on December Saturday afternoons, and Mrs. Claus visits on Second Sunday Funday.
kidfact: Irving's birthday is in Christmas week: the town started with a land sale on December 19, 1903, six days before Christmas.
faq: When is the Irving Christmas parade?

The City of Irving holds its Holidays at Heritage parade on the first Saturday of the season in the Heritage District downtown. In 2026 it is Saturday, December 5, at 6 pm, with activities in Heritage Park afterward and the tree lighting and a drone light show at 8:30 pm. The city lists Holidays at Heritage as free.
Where can kids see Santa for free in Irving?

Santa visits Irving Arts Center on December Saturday afternoons for free card and craft making, and on December 19 he sits at the Heritage Park gazebo, where the City of Irving gives families a free printed and digital photo. Mrs. Claus visits the arts center during Second Sunday Funday.
Can we take the train to Irving's Christmas events?

Yes. The Trinity Railway Express stops at the Downtown Irving/Heritage Crossing station at 201 Rock Island Road, a short walk from Heritage Park and the Holidays at Heritage parade, tree lighting and Santa morning. The DART Orange Line serves Las Colinas, home of Irving Arts Center and the Mandalay Canal.
What is the Holiday Tree Exhibition?

It is Irving Arts Center's yearly display of decorated Christmas trees in its free galleries, open Tuesday through Saturday in December. In 2026 it reached its 34th year with the theme Holiday Time Machine. The trees are posted on Facebook, and the one with the most likes wins its decorators a cash prize.
Why is Irving's history tied to trains?

Irving's founders, J.O. Schulze and Otis Brown, were surveyors for the Chicago, Rock Island and Gulf Railway when they picked the spot for a town along the line in 1902. Heritage Park keeps a replica of the 1903 Rock Island Depot, and commuter trains still stop nearby today.
